statement: A $2026 \times 2026$ board is \textit{bordeaux} if at least one cell is red. A rectangular region is \textit{oddly-rectangular} if it contains an odd number of red cells. Find the largest $M$ such that every bordeaux board contains an oddly-rectangular region of at least $M$ cells.

Marie starts with 1. She may replace $V$ with $j \cdot R(V/j)$ for $1 \leq j \leq n$, where $R(x)$ rounds to nearest integer (half-integers up). (a) Prove there exists $B$ such that Marie can never exceed $B$. (b) Show there exists $N$ such that $2026 \mid f(n)$ for all $n \geq N$, where $f(n)$ is the maximum achievable.
Find all $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f\!\left((f(x)+f(y))^2\right) = (x+y)f(x+y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$.
Let $1 = a_1 \geq a_2 \geq \cdots$ be reals with $a_n = a_{2n} + a_{2n+1}$ for all $n \geq 1$. For $r = 2026^{2026}$, prove $\dfrac{1}{r} \leq a_r \leq \dfrac{2}{r+1}$.

Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AC > AB$, circumcircle $\omega$, circumcenter $O$. $K$ = intersection of tangents at $B$, $C$. Circle $ABK$ meets $BC$ again at $Z \neq B$. $L$ = midpoint of $KZ$, $X = KZ \cap AB$. $V$ on circle $ABL$ on same side of $BC$ as $A$ with $OV \perp KZ$. Prove $LV \perp CX$.

Let $p$ be prime and $p \nmid n$. Let $k = \tau(n)$ and $1 = d_1 < \cdots < d_k = n$ the divisors of $n$. For each $i$, let $c_i$ count divisors $\ell$ of $d_i^2$ with $p \mid d_i - \ell$. Prove $(p-1)(c_1 + \cdots + c_k) \geq k^2$.
